item.title: Tailored ZnO/Cellulose Separator Reconfigures Solvation Chemistry for Durable Magnesium Metal Batteries
item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work introduces a ZnO/cellulose composite separator that anchors solvent molecules via bidirectional charge transfer, reconfiguring Mg²⁺ solvation into a single-cluster structure. This enables a dense, inorganic-rich SEI, achieving over 2000 h cycling in Mg||Mg cells. The inorganic inter-reinforced organic strategy offers a generalizable route to durable, high-safety magnesium metal batteries.

Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work identifies Zn anode polarization and short-circuiting—not sulfur loss—as the dominant failure mode in iodine-mediated Zn–S batteries. Guided by this diagnosis, iodoacetamide couples interphase and solvation regulation, forming a gradient interphase and modulating Zn2+ coordination. The result is 2000-cycle Zn||Cu stability and 75.95% capacity retention over 550 cycles, offering a practical design principle for durable aqueous Zn–S batteries.

Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work reveals diluent conformational flexibility as a new molecular design dimension controlling instantaneous solvation-state distributions, beyond conventional coordination numbers. Flexible diluents create rich, uniform solvation states, boosting exchange current density and interfacial kinetics.
